5b1a799740864196c7cc5093eed71ea42a28f52d.summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 analyses TuxBot v3 Evolution, a previously undocumented modular IoT botnet framework with Telnet brute-forcing, several C2 channels, a DDoS-for-hire panel and builds for 17 architectures. The developer relied on an LLM, which left reasoning comments in the code and hallucinated a password-hashing implementation. Many features are broken, but the report says fixed versions likely exist in the wild. Infrastructure links the framework to Keksec/Kaitori and AISURU tooling.

5b29f671666c9e98a0fb600a486b2ae9dfaf9188.summary: Elastic Security Labs analysis, published 2024-12-12, of PUMAKIT, a multi-stage Linux malware. A dropper disguised as a cron binary runs memory-resident executables, one of which loads PUMA, an LKM kernel rootkit. A shared-object userland rootkit called Kitsune is embedded in the kernel module. The rootkit hooks 18 syscalls with ftrace to hide files, directories and itself, escalates privileges through a special hook, and communicates with C2 servers. Elastic provides detection queries and a YARA signature. The report names no threat actor or country.
